title: R Commands for Causal Inference
text: gives histograms comparing quality life hormone treatment control. gives density plot proposensity score (ps).
code:
plot.qol <- ggplot(bcrot, aes(x=qol, after_stat(density)), fill=as.factor(hormon)) +     geom_histogram(aes(fill=as.factor(hormon)), color=c("#e9ecef"), binwidth = 2) +     facet_grid(as.factor(hormon) ~ .) +     labs(x = "Quality of life", y = "Density") +     scale_fill_manual(values=c("#69b3a2", "#337CA0"),                       name="Hormonal
treatment",                       breaks=c("0", "1"),                       labels=c("no", "yes")) +     theme_light() plot.qol # plot density ggplot(bcrot, aes(ps, fill = as.factor(hormon))) +   geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +   labs(x = "Propensity score",        y = "Density",        fill = "Hormone
treatment") +   scale_fill_manual(values=c("#69b3a2", "#337CA0"),                     name="Hormonal
treatment",                     breaks=c("0", "1"),                     labels=c("no", "yes")) +   theme_light()

title: R Commands for Causal Inference
code: fit <- glm(qol ~ hormon*age + XXXX,  ## fill in other variables!            data = bcrot2) fit.std <- stdGlm(fit = fit, data = as.data.frame(bcrot2), X = "hormon") print(summary(fit.std)) plot(fit.std)  # Confidence interval: Mean difference  summary(fit.std, contrast = "difference", reference = "0")

title: R Commands for Causal Inference
code: # Build SuperLearner libraries for outcome (Q) and exposure models (g) sl.lib <- c("SL.mean","SL.glm")    # Construct an aipw object for later estimations  AIPW_SL <- AIPW::AIPW$new(Y = bcrot2$qol,                           A = bcrot2$hormon_i,                           W = subset(bcrot2, select = c(XXX)),   # fill in!                           Q.SL.library = sl.lib,                           g.SL.library = sl.lib,                           k_split = 10,                           verbose = TRUE)  # Fit the data to the AIPW object and check the balance of propensity scores raipw <- AIPW_SL$fit()$summary() AIPW_SL$fit()$plot.p_score()$plot.ip_weights()  # Truncate weights (default truncation is set to 0.025) AIPW_SL$fit()$summary(g.bound = c(0.05, 0.95))$plot.p_score()$plot.ip_weights()  # Calculate average treatment effects among the treated/untreated (controls) (ATT/ATC) AIPW_SL$stratified_fit()$summary()   # extract weights for loveplots # AIPW_SL$plot.ip_weights() bcrot2$aipw <- AIPW_SL$ip_weights.plot$data$ip_weights

title: Installation: Step-by-step
text: Package installation github requires authentification. already installed GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT), go subsection 3. Otherwise proceed follows: 1. Generate Personal Access Token (PAT) Go [GitHub → Settings → Developer Settings → Personal Access Tokens → Tokens (classic)]. Click “Generate new token (classic)”. Give token descriptive name (e.g., R package installation). repo accessing private repositories, read:packages Click Generate token. Copy token immediately keep somewhere secure — won’t see . 2. Configure PAT R Install usethis already installed, run: opens personal .Renviron file. Add following line: Replace your_personal_access_token_here actual token. Save file restart RStudio. can check whether R can access token 3. Install package GitHub Install pak necessary: 4. Load package
code: install.packages("usethis")    usethis::edit_r_environ() GITHUB_PAT=your_personal_access_token_here Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT") # during installation: plz update all packages!!! install.packages("pak") options(pkg.build_vignettes = TRUE) # important to build the vignette pak::pkg_install("bips-hb/APTS_Causal_Inference") # load package library(APTSCausalInference)  # Load the example data data(bcrot)
